precepts.text: David smote Moab and measured them with a line, so that Moab became David's servants and brought gifts, that is, tribute, when Israel served the Lord.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
David “smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground”, and “so the Moabites became David’s servants, and brought gifts.” Those gifts are tribute. Moab was subdued under Israel when Israel served the Lord.

So when “Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab”, it shows the change. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

precepts.text: If Israel hearkens diligently to the voice of the Lord to do his commandments, the Most High will set them on high above all nations of the earth, as happened under David.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments”, then “the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.”

That is what happened under David, when Moab and the other nations were brought under Israel. Being set on high above the nations depends on hearkening to the voice of the Lord. After Ahab, Israel was not hearkening, and so Moab no longer stayed beneath them.

precepts.text: The Lord causes the enemies that rise up against Israel to be smitten before their face when the nation keeps his commandments.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

When Israel keeps his commandments, the enemies that rise up are smitten before them, as Moab was smitten under David. Moab rising up and rebelling after the death of Ahab shows that the nation was no longer under that blessing.

precepts.text: But if Israel will not hearken to the voice of the Lord to do his commandments, all these curses shall come upon them and overtake them.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

The same chapter that promised to set Israel on high above all nations promised the curses if they would not hearken. Under Ahab they did not, and the curses began to overtake them. Moab breaking away is part of that.

precepts.text: The Lord causes a disobedient Israel to be smitten before their enemies and scattered, their carcasses meat for the fowls of the air, which is the same judgment pronounced on the house of Ahab.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth. And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.”

This is the blessing of verse 7 turned around. Instead of the enemy fleeing seven ways before Israel, a disobedient Israel flees seven ways before the enemy and is scattered. And the carcase given as meat for the fowls of the air is the same judgment pronounced on the house of Ahab. After Ahab’s death Moab rebels, and the curse is on its way.

precepts.text: When the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out that it had been brought to slay them, for the hand of God was heavy there, so the god of Ekron could not even defend his own people against the God of Israel.
precepts.point: When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
When the ark of God was sent to Ekron, “the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.” They begged to send it away, “for there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.”

The god of Ekron could not even defend his own people against the God of Israel. That is Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, the one Ahaziah sent to when he fell through the lattice and was sick.

Ahaziah should have known that history, and it would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron. That is why Elijah asks, “Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron?” He turned to an idol rather than the Most High, and the word came: “thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.”

precepts.text: He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins; and he said, It is Elijah the Tishbite.
precepts.point: His raiment of camel's hair and the leathern girdle about his loins are not incidental. That was Elijah's manner, and it marks John as coming in the same spirit.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John's raiment of camel's hair and the leathern girdle about his loins are not incidental. When the messengers described the man who met them, “He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins”, the king knew at once: “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”

That was Elijah's manner, the hairy garment and the girdle of leather about his loins. John wore the same, and it marks him as coming in the same spirit, the Elijah sent before the coming of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: Ahaziah falls down through a lattice in his upper chamber and is sick, and sends messengers to inquire of Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, whether he shall recover. He turns to an idol rather than to the Most High for his answer.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: The angel of the Lord sends Elijah the Tishbite to meet the messengers and ask whether it is because there is no God in Israel that they go to inquire of Beelzebub. The word of the Lord is that Ahaziah shall not come down from his bed but shall surely die.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: The king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to Elijah, who sits on the top of a hill, and the captain commands the man of God to come down. Elijah answers that if he is a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume him and his fifty, and it does.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: A second captain of fifty is sent and speaks the same way, and fire from heaven consumes him and his fifty as well. The third captain goes up, falls on his knees, and pleads that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in Elijah's sight.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: The angel of the Lord tells Elijah to go down with the third captain and not to fear him. Elijah delivers to the king the same word, that because he sent to inquire of Beelzebub as though there were no God in Israel, he shall surely die.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: Ahaziah dies according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram reigns in his stead because Ahaziah had no son. The rest of the acts of Ahaziah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
